svg.title: Scene 58: Frequency, wavelength and phase
svg.desc: Five frames about classical waves. 1, one wave with its wavelength (crest to crest), its amplitude (height) and what frequency and phase mean. 2 to 5, two equal waves added with the second shifted by a phase of 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees; each panel plots both inputs and their computed sum, whose amplitude is 2.00, 1.41, 0.00 and 1.41 times one wave’s, and whose intensity, proportional to amplitude squared, is 4.00, 2.00, 0.00 and 2.00. A note says that amplitude is height while energy goes with amplitude squared.
svg.text: Shift one wave against the other and the sum

g.text: Phase φ: where in its cycle a wave is, 0° to 360°.
Blue: wave A. Light blue dashed: wave B.
Dark: their sum, computed point by point.
Amplitude is height; the energy a wave carries goes as
amplitude². In a real pond, energy missing at quiet
spots shows up at loud ones.
